strategy.title: No plan yet: subcontracted refrigerant leak-rate inspections lack an established cost
strategy.why: Buyer, price ($800, evidenced), close rate (5 of 40 on this offer), volume (175 stores, annual need) and 10-day settlement are established, but the named subcontractor's quoted cost and payment terms are not on the record, so neither the margin nor the no-up-front-capital limit can be shown to hold.

alternatives.title: Sell 6 inspections at $800 via the association directory, fulfilled by the quoted subcontractor
alternatives.why: Would carry $4,800 against the $4,000 target once the subcontractor's per-inspection cost is shown below $800 and payable from the buyer's payment (no advance).

steps.label: Obtain the named subcontractor's quoted price per inspection and its payment terms (whether any deposit is due before the buyer pays)

sources.population: Independent grocery store owners contacted for this offer

sources.claim: 175 stores in the state association directory, annual inspection need
A named subcontractor quoted to do the work (amount not recorded)

noPlan.decisiveGap: The subcontractor's cost per inspection and payment terms are not recorded: the card names a quoted subcontractor but no direct cost, so the deal's margin and whether it needs money advanced before the buyer pays are unknown.
noPlan.resolution: Get the subcontractor's written quote (per-inspection price and when it is due); if it is under $800 and payable after the buyer pays, sell 6 inspections to the directory stores at the measured 1-in-8 close rate (about 48 contacts).

review.reasons: NO_PLAN with ECONOMICS as the decisive gap is right. Price $800, conversion of 5 in 40 measured on this offer, 175 stores with a yearly need, a quoted subcontractor as fulfiller and 10-day settlement are all evidence. The card has no direct-cost figure for the subcontractor, so the margin is unknown. That is decided by obtaining the quote, not by a live test, and it is not a ceiling. I recomputed: 6 x $800 = $4,800 against $4,000, and 6 / 0.125 = 48 contacts, well inside 175.
findings: Overly conservative: 'capital advanced before buyer payment' is marked UNKNOWN, but the card holds exposure $0 as EVIDENCE (and $0 peak funding). Only the per-inspection cost is genuinely missing

Not stated: if the subcontractor's cost is close to $800, more than 6 sales are needed for the settled cash net of fulfilment to reach $4,000. The resolution should recompute the deal count from the quote
